criteria.name: Problem 6
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6 (3 pts). Statement: 6. Given the sequence{an}, prove that each entry of the corresponding triangular array is given by the formula Tn,k = k∑ i=0 (k i ) an−i where (k i ) is the usual binomial coeﬃcient (k i ) = k! i!(k−i)!. You may use standard facts about the binomial coeﬃcients in your proof.

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (2 pts). Statement: 7. Given a sequence {bn}, prove that there is a unique sequence {an} whose triangular transform is{bn}. The sequence {an} will be called the inverse triangular transform of{bn}.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (1 pt). Statement: 8. Given a sequence {bn} of integers, prove that its inverse triangular transform is also a sequence of integers.

criteria.name: Problem 9
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9 (2 pts). Statement: 9. Given a sequence{bn}, prove that there is a unique sequence{an} whose boustrophedon transform is{bn}. The sequence{ab} will be called the inverse boustrophedon transform of{bn}.

criteria.name: Problem 10
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10 (1 pt). Statement: 10. Prove that the inverse boustrophedon transform of a sequence of integers is again a sequence of integers.

criteria.name: Problem 11
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 11 (2 pts). Statement: 11. There are ﬁve up-down permutations of the ﬁrst 4 positive integers. List them.

criteria.name: Problem 12
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12 (2 pts). Statement: 12. Compute the number of up-down permutation of the ﬁrst 5 positive integers.

criteria.name: Problem 13
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 13 (2 pts). Statement: 13. Prove that the number of up-down permutations of the ﬁrst n positive integers and the number of down-up permutations of the ﬁrst n positive integers are equal.

criteria.name: Problem 14
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 14 (3 pts). Statement: 14. Let An be the number of up-down permutations of the ﬁrst n positive integers. For example, there are two up-down permutations of the ﬁrst three positive integers: ⟨⟨1, 3, 2⟩⟩ and⟨⟨2, 3, 1⟩⟩. The sequence {An} begins 1, 1, 1, 2, 5,... where the next term is the correct answer to the previous problem, and the “empty permutation” of the ﬁrst 0 positive integers is declared by deﬁnition to be an up-down permutation. Prove that An satisﬁes the recurrence relation 2An+1 = n∑ k=0 (n k ) AkAn−k (with, of course, the initial value A0 = 1).
